en_excerpt_original: 「I’ll be home late today.」 True to those words, my shift ended and I got home late—well past a reasonable dinner hour. Naturally, Miyagi wasn’t in the shared living space. I turned on the lights and the air conditioner, then knocked twice on the door I’d knocked on before leaving the apartment and called out to her. 「Miyagi, I’m back. I’m going to make dinner, so just wait a little longer.」 Not that she’d come out anyway. Without waiting for a reply, I went to my room to drop off my coat and bag. When I opened the fridge, I felt relieved to see the fried rice I’d made for lunch was gone. Skipping one meal probably wouldn’t make her collapse or anything, but eating was still better than not eating. I checked the rice cooker and, as expected, there was no rice ready. I filled a pot with water and set it on the stove, then got out the pasta and took vegetables from the fridge to make a salad. I decided to use a store-bought sauce, so I shredded some cabbage, cut up a tomato, and added salt to the boiling water. Just as I put the pasta in the pot and set the timer, I felt eyes on me and turned around. I had no idea when she’d come out of her room, but my eyes met Miyagi’s. 「It’s not ready yet, so you can wait in your room if you want. I’ll call you when it’s done.」 I called out to Miyagi, who was standing in front of her door, and she averted her gaze. 「I’ll wait here.」 「If you’re going to wait, at least sit down.」 I had no idea what she was thinking, but she didn’t answer. Still, whether she was standing or sitting, I’d rather have her in the same space as me, so I turned my back to her and heated up the meat sauce. After a while, I heard the sound of a chair scraping against the floor, and I thought once again that Miyagi really did resemble a stray cat. She’d run away if I got too close, but then she’d also come near me on a whim. I figured there was probably no such thing as a “proper distance” between me and Miyagi. Every distance was both right and wrong. Which was why Miyagi, who’d been hiding under her covers like a lump before I left for work, was now staring at me so hard I could feel her glare boring into my back. It felt way too capricious, but a Miyagi who wasn’t capricious wouldn’t be Miyagi at all. I plated the cabbage and tomato, then turned around. 「What are you doing, Miyagi?」 「Nothing.」 She replied curtly, her gaze dropping to the table. Yep, definitely capricious. As I stood there wondering if I should say something else to her now that she’d stopped looking at me, the timer went off. I silenced the insistent electronic beeping, drained the pasta into a colander, plated it, and poured the meat sauce over it. 「Sorry to keep you waiting.」 I set the pasta and salad on the table and handed her a fork. 「Thanks. Let’s eat.」 Miyagi said flatly, twirling the pasta around her fork. Then she ate in silence, one bite, then another. Watching her sit there quietly eating her pasta—the same Miyagi who’d been nothing but a lump under the covers earlier today—made the phrase “successfully tamed” float through my mind, and she looked more and more like a stray cat. The dry clinking of forks and plates echoed through the otherwise silent shared living space. The pasta, which I’d made extra of, steadily disappeared, half of it vanishing in no time. Even so, I couldn’t help thinking Miyagi was terrible at eating pasta. The amount she twirled onto her fork was always either too much or too little. She’d stuff a huge clump into her mouth and chew and chew, or she’d eat a pitifully small bite with an unsatisfied look on her face, so I never got tired of watching her. If I told her to her face that I found that side of her cute, she’d get mad. And if I told her outright that she was bad at eating pasta, she’d get mad at that too. But since she’d get mad either way, maybe I could get away with saying she was cute—though I had a feeling that if I made her mad today, she’d retreat to her room, so I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat. There’d be other chances to call her cute later. For now, I was better off not saying anything unnecessary. 「Is it good?」 I threw out something neutral and easy to answer. 「It’s good.」 Miyagi answered without looking at me. 「What were you planning to do for dinner if I hadn’t come home?」 This time I asked a question I wasn’t sure she’d answer, and Miyagi’s hand, which had been twirling the pasta, stopped.
